key_insight: For slide-level ovarian serous carcinoma grading, pretrained MobileNet performed best, while adding spatial attention to channel attention showed no detectable benefit.
clinical_relevance: Distinguishing high-grade from low-grade serous carcinoma could support pathology workflows, but this study evaluates classification—not drug discovery or clinical readiness.
method: Compared CNN attention variants, pretrained MobileNet with differential attention, and a Phikon foundation-model benchmark.
Used stain normalisation, slide-level pooling, and five-fold slide-grouped cross-validation to prevent slide leakage.
Evaluated three training seeds with within-fold threshold selection and multiplicity-corrected statistical comparisons.
evidence_signal: On 259 UBC-OCEAN slides (217 high-grade, 42 low-grade), pretrained MobileNet achieved AUC 0.862 ± 0.005 and MCC 0.460, outperforming the no-attention baseline and Squeeze-and-Excitation model.
watch_item: The imbalanced, single-cohort evaluation and colour-only AUC of 0.66 warrant external validation for stain-related confounding and generalisability.
paper_title: Which Attention Helps? A Slide-Level Ablation of Attention-Augmented CNNs for Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Grading
